paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “QAdapter” visually compares the GPU memory consumption, measured in gigabytes (GB), across six different fine-tuning methods for the Llama-3-8B model on ten NLP tasks, as evaluated in the context of the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical y-axis represents GPU Memory (GB), scaled linearly from 0 to approximately 70, with labeled tick marks at 0, 20, 40, and 60. The horizontal x-axis lists the six methods: “Full FT,” “MTL-FT,” “TAG,” “Adapter,” “QAdapter,” and “Ours,” presented in that left-to-right order without explicit sorting by value. Five of the bars are colored orange, while the final bar, labeled “Ours,” is distinctly colored green. The “Full FT” method exhibits the highest GPU memory usage, with a bar reaching approximately 70 GB. “MTL-FT” follows with a value around 43 GB, “TAG” and “Adapter” are comparable at roughly 20 GB each, and “QAdapter” consumes the least among the orange bars at approximately 10 GB. The “Ours” method, highlighted in green, uses about 20 GB of GPU memory, matching the “TAG” and “Adapter” methods. No error bars, annotations, or additional visual emphasis beyond color differentiation for “Ours” are present.
